comments.comment:
I would agree, except the project has already accepted LLM generated code into base via tmux. For all of Theo's objections to LLM code in OpenBSD due to licensing and code quality issues, vibe-coded tmux releases are now a part of base. Any questions about this posed to Theo or other project leaders continue to go unanswered and unacknowledged.

That extremely loud silence on their part was enough to make me move on from using OpenBSD.

comments.comment:
I have no good counter-argument to the other commenter, but I don't think your acquaintances stance is at all relevant to how OpenBSD behaves. They have always had a somewhat inflammatory humour, be that using Comic Sans in their presentations or having "This directory contains software that is Gigantic and Nasty but Unavoidable." in the gnu/ subfolder's README.

in contrast, this here is an animation someone used to proclaim "i made something new and shiny", not a shitpost at all.

Strong disagree. The OpenBSD cover art and song were always used to celebrate human art. The fact that in the same place now stands the sloppiest slop imaginable, paired with a blatantly anti-AI song makes it clear that this is satire and meant to evoke negative feelings towards genAI taking space away from human art.
